general_information.Description: The course is designed to consolidate and enhance students' grammatical knowledge. It aims to achieve this by giving learners exposure to grammar as it is used in real life situations, offering them comprehensive explanations for grammatical forms and meanings, providing contextualized practice of various structures, and developing their use of such structures as well as their critical thinking skills through communicative activities. Students will also be informed of how to recognize common grammatical errors in their written work and encouraged to apply learned grammar in writing. Utilizing a flipped classroom approach, they will engage with core grammar concepts and materials independently before class sessions. They are also encouraged to leverage AI tools as resources to support their grammar learning, practice, and writing processes.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes
general_information.Note: Progress marks: - 02 Mini Projects: 30% - 03 Progress tests: 30% Final exam: 40% Conditions to pass: Each on-going assessment's component's mark: >=3/10 Each progress tests' components' mark >0 Each final exam's components' mark >0 Final exam's mark: >=4/10 Grade average >=5/10

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze how grammar is used in many contexts from a variety of reading and listening texts
Assess whether structures being used are appropriate for written and spoken communication

Compose grammatically accurate spoken and written texts of different topics CLO3.1: Recall basic and advanced structures of English and their meanings CLO3.2: Identify and correct common grammatical errors in both written and spoken English CLO3.3: Explain how and why basic and advanced structures of English are used in different contexts
Proactively collaborate with peers for group work and problem-solving
Critically and ethically use AI tools to support grammar learning.

assessments.Question Type: - From week 3, students work in groups of 5 to: + Choose 2 units from the units taught in the course. + Conduct peer-teaching sessions. For these sessions, they prepare interactive activities to help their classmates review and practice the grammatical structures from the Grammar Notes section of these units . Suggested Peer-Teaching Activities: + Grammar quizzes or “Find the error” challenges + Role-plays or dialogues using the target structure + Mini grammar games (e.g., Kahoot, Jeopardy, sentence race) + Sentence-combining or transformation tasks + Short group writing or storytelling using the grammar point + Peer-correction or editing activities *Students are encouraged to use AI tools to assist with this project. Any use of AI tools must be clearly documented in the project report submitted to the lecturer. Potential uses include: + Generate examples for the target grammar point + Create quiz items, dialogues, or game questions + Get feedback on lesson plans or activity instructions + Other purposes

assessments.Question Type: *Option 1: Students work in a group of 5: - Each group contacts lecturers of ENT/TRS classes, BEN's writing classes (EAW, ERW, ENB) or ENM classes to ask for 3 pieces of writing (paragraphs, essays or emails) in which grammatical errors are largely present. - Each member in a group is in charge of identifying any grammatical errors in the 3 pieces of writing obtained. - Each group writes a booklet for EFL learners. In the booklet, they select the most common grammatical errors (at least 5) from the pieces of writing, put forward suggestions on how to avoid them, and design some exercises to help the readers practice writing sentences/paragraphs with the relevant grammatical structures. - The groups send their booklets to the lecturer in charge for marking and give a presentation on how they have worked on the booklet in class for feedback. - The lecturer in charge can invite other lecturers to come to the class, and the groups can pitch the booklet to them. *Students are encouraged to use AI tools to assist with this project. Any use of AI tools must be clearly documented in the project report submitted to the lecturer. Potential uses include: + Error Identification: Students can first identify grammatical errors manually and then use AI tools to perform the same task. This allows them to compare their own findings with the AI's suggestions. + Researching Explanations: They can use AI tools to find reliable materials that come with grammatical explanations, which will help them write the section on how to avoid common errors. + Designing Exercises: They can use AI tools to generate draft exercises for the booklet, which they must then review and adjust for suitability and accuracy. + Other Purposes. *Option 2: Lecturer’s choice

schedule.Student's Tasks: These activities can be performed throughout Weeks 1–2 so that students can achieve the AI-integration learning outcome by Session 12: - Compare and contrast AI’s explanations to advanced grammatical structures when using different prompting techniques - Compare and contrast AI’s examples when using different prompting techniques Suggested prompting techniques for the activities: + Zero-shot prompting: Give AI a direct, no-example request. + Few-shot prompting: Provide a few examples within the prompt to guide AI on the desired format or style. + One-shot prompting: A specific type of few-shot prompting where only one example is given. + Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: Break down complex problems into smaller, sequential steps to guide the model through a logical process. + Contextual prompting: Provide extra background information and details to improve AI's understanding.
